title: Excision of a skin lesion
summary: Elliptical excision biopsy of a forearm lesion under local anaesthetic.

steps.title: Introduce yourself and check identity
steps.prompt: Hello… are you the doctor doing my operation?

choices.text: Hello, I'm one of the surgical team. Can you tell me your full name and date of birth?
Yes. Let's get started straight away.
choices.feedback: Introduce yourself and confirm identity first.

steps.hint: Name, role, then two identifiers from the patient, checked against the wristband.

steps.title: Explain and check understanding
steps.prompt: What exactly are you going to do?

choices.text: I'll explain the excision of the lump, why we're doing it, the main risks such as a scar, bleeding and the need for further surgery if the result shows it, and the alternatives. Stop me with any questions.
choices.reply: Thank you. That helps. What about the pain afterwards?

choices.text: It's a routine thing, nothing to worry about.
choices.feedback: Material risks and alternatives must be explained.

steps.hint: Valid consent: capacity, information (nature, purpose, material risks, alternatives), voluntary decision.

steps.title: Pick up the marking pen
steps.hint: Mark the ellipse before the local anaesthetic distorts the skin.

steps.title: Mark a 3:1 ellipse along the skin tension lines
steps.hint: Margins of 2 mm for a benign-looking lesion.

steps.title: Pick up the skin preparation
steps.hint: Alcoholic chlorhexidine, applied from the incision site outwards.

steps.title: Prepare the skin over the lesion
steps.hint: Centre outwards, wider than the incision; let it dry fully before drapes and diathermy (it is flammable).

steps.title: Draw up local anaesthetic
steps.hint: 1 % lidocaine; check the maximum safe dose for the patient's weight first.

steps.title: Infiltrate the ellipse
steps.hint: Aspirate before injecting; wait for the anaesthetic to work.

steps.title: Incise along the ellipse
steps.hint: Blade perpendicular to the skin, through the full dermis.

steps.title: Excise the ellipse at the level of the subcutaneous fat
steps.hint: Hold the tip with toothed forceps; don't crush the specimen.

steps.title: Put the specimen in the specimen pot
steps.hint: Label it at the bedside: patient, site, date, orientation.

steps.title: Specimen labelling
steps.prompt: When should the specimen be labelled?

choices.text: Immediately, at the bedside, with the patient's identifiers
At the end of the list

choices.feedback: They cannot know whose it is.

steps.title: Close with interrupted sutures and dress
steps.hint: As in the wound closure lab.
